rv.q: Yet The Other Place, like many other attempts to modernize the Greeks, has a hole where the ancient gods, fates and rituals should be.
Thanks to the superb performances and the playwright’s riveting staging you’re mesmerized for every one of its concise 80 minutes.
“The Other Place” is at its best an intensely acted exploration of grief and family dynamics.
Ultimately, Zeldin's sensationalistic conclusion feels hollow: it's earnestly performed and entirely insubstantial.
A multisensory Greek tragedy disguised as a house renovation, The Other Place descends into family dysfunction with haunting inevitability.
This first-class production has had the smarts to bring its two leads across the pond.

cn.t: Critics give mixed reviews to Zeldin's modern family drama inspired by Antigone, praising D'Arcy's commanding performance but finding the play itself underfed and struggling to balance its Greek tragedy roots with contemporary domestic conflict.
